questions.q: In Vitruvian intercolumniation, a spacing of two column diameters is:
questions.n: Pycnostyle 1.5D, systyle 2D, eustyle 2.25D, diastyle 3D, araeostyle wider.

questions.q: The Roman architect-engineer who wrote De architectura in the 1st century BC:
questions.n: Marcus Vitruvius Pollio.

questions.q: "Always design a thing by considering it in its next larger context" is attributed to:
questions.n: The father, Eliel, not his son Eero.

questions.q: Gaudí's Sagrada Família blends:
o: Gothic revival with organic, nature-based forms
questions.n: Gothic structure reinterpreted through natural geometry.

questions.q: "There is nothing in a caterpillar that tells you it's going to be a butterfly." Who said it?
questions.n: Fuller, inventor of the geodesic dome.

questions.q: A dry-stone hut with a corbelled conical roof, as in Apulia's trulli, is a:
questions.n: Corbelled stone forms a beehive dome.

questions.q: The conical Plains dwelling of poles covered with hides is the:
questions.n: Tepees are portable; wigwams are domed.

questions.q: Originally a hunting lodge, enlarged by Louis XIV, with a Hall of Mirrors and gardens by Le Nôtre:
questions.n: Versailles became the seat of French royal power.

questions.q: The Art Deco Capitol Theater in Manila, with its rare double balcony, was designed by:
questions.n: Nakpil, later a National Artist.

questions.q: The Navajo dwelling built of logs and covered with earth is the:
questions.n: Hogans are domed log-and-earth houses.

questions.q: "Architecture is the will of an epoch translated into space." Who?
questions.n: Mies, 1920s.

questions.q: The White House was designed by:
questions.n: Irish-born Hoban won the 1792 competition.

questions.q: Calling for things "organically suited to the little man in the street," this Finnish architect was:
questions.n: Aalto's humanist modernism.

questions.q: "I believe in God, only I spell it Nature." Who?
questions.n: Wright, the champion of organic architecture.

questions.q: The Padre Pio Pilgrimage Church in San Giovanni Rotondo was designed by:
questions.n: Completed in 2004.

questions.q: "Architecture is the masterly, correct and magnificent play of masses brought together in light." Who?
questions.n: From Towards a New Architecture.

questions.q: Which Finnish modernist designed buildings, bentwood furniture and glassware, using local materials with a human touch?
questions.n: Paimio chairs and Savoy vases are his.

questions.q: Doric on the ground floor, Ionic above, Corinthian on top: this stacking is called:
questions.n: Superposed orders go from heaviest to lightest upward.

questions.q: Bernini, not Borromini, sculpted which Baroque masterpiece?
questions.n: It's in the Cornaro Chapel; the churches listed are Borromini's.

questions.q: The Bahá'í Lotus Temple is in:
questions.n: Designed by Fariborz Sahba, completed 1986.
